judged_text: Rewriting `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` as `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the condition, so the slug is now written exactly in the cases where it previously was not. On instances with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false (self-hosted), organizations are created with no slug at all — Organization.slug is a required unique column, so the Prisma create throws and every organization creation fails with a 500; with billing enabled, orgs get their slug immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug verification flow that the very next line still encodes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips the condition: `slug` is now written when team billing *is enabled* instead of when it is disabled. The next line still writes `metadata.requestedSlug` only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, so with billing enabled the code now sets both `slug` and `requestedSlug`, whereas previously it did not set `slug` in that branch. With billing disabled, `slug` is no longer provided at all by this handler. This is a concrete behavioral inversion introduced by the diff and can break org creation if `slug` is required.
